questions.question: What color are temporary signs in construction and maintenance work areas?

options.text: Red background with green writing.
Orange background with black writing.
Yellow background with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange background with black writing.
questions.explanation: Temporary signs in work zones have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off these weather conditions and reduce visibility.

questions.question: When crossing a sidewalk while entering or exiting a driveway, what should drivers do?

options.text: Have the right-of-way.
Yield to pedestrians.
Honk at pedestrians to clear a path.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians when crossing a sidewalk to enter or exit a driveway, alley, or parking lot.

questions.question: Who can use handicap parking spaces?

options.text: Anyone, but only if all other spaces are full.
Only drivers with the appropriate license plate or hanging tag.
People who are not feeling well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only drivers with the appropriate license plate or hanging tag.
questions.explanation: Handicap parking spaces are for people with disabilities who have the correct license plate or hanging tag displaying the international symbol.

questions.question: What should drivers use to improve visibility in rain or fog?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off bad weather and reduce visibility.

questions.question: Where should a driver look while driving?

options.text: Straight ahead only.
Only at the center of the road.
To the sides, ahead, and behind the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the sides, ahead, and behind the car.
questions.explanation: Good drivers watch all around their vehicle to know what is happening in every direction.

questions.question: If you drink several beers, how can you reduce the effects of alcohol?

options.text: Take a cold shower.
Wait several hours.
Drink several cups of coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait several hours.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Cold showers and coffee do not speed up this process. It takes about one hour to remove the effects of one drink.

questions.question: A school bus ahead of you has flashing red lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and proceed when you think children have exited.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop until the red lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the red lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. Exception: You do not need to stop if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.

questions.question: How should you change lanes?

options.text: Quickly and often.
When a car is in your blind spot.
Gradually and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually and carefully.
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and carefully, only when necessary. Every lane change increases the risk of an accident.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights approaches?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Try to reach your destination before it arrives.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: Law requires drivers to pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances using sirens and flashing lights. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first.

questions.question: What happens as blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases?

options.text: You become more intoxicated.
You become more sober.
You become more coordinated.

questions.correctAnswerText: You become more intoxicated.
questions.explanation: BAC measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. Higher BAC means more impairment.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags, should seat belts still be worn?

options.text: Yes, seat belts should still be worn.
No, seat belts are not needed.
Seat belts should be worn behind the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags and seat belts work together for the best protection in a crash.

questions.question: If you become drowsy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Fight the drowsiness.
Take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: Stop at a rest area or service station to take a break, nap, stretch, or switch drivers. Caffeine pills are not a good substitute for rest and can make driving more dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead has many curves.
There is a sharp curve in the road ahead.
The road ahead may be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead may be slippery.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: If a traffic signal light is green and a police officer signals for you to stop, what should you do?

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic signal.
Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: You must obey a police officer's directions, even if they conflict with traffic signals, signs, or markings.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a 35 mph speed zone after the curve ahead.
Drive no slower than 35 mph around the upcoming curve.
Slow down to 35 mph or less before the upcoming curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to 35 mph or less before the upcoming curve.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to upcoming road conditions. The speed shown is the recommended safe speed for that curve.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Closer behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: Stay farther back from large trucks because they have large blind spots and need more distance to stop.

questions.question: What does a steady green traffic light mean?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Adjust your mirrors.
You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can proceed through the intersection if it is safe. Always check for pedestrians and other traffic already in the intersection.

questions.question: If you must stop on an interstate highway, what should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn to warn other drivers.
Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first passing car.
Pull off the road, turn on your hazard lights, and stay in your vehicle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on your hazard lights, and stay in your vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: Pull onto the shoulder, use hazard lights to warn others, and stay inside your vehicle. Standing on an interstate is very dangerous due to fast-moving traffic.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area designated for road construction workers.
The area where pedestrians cross the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The area where pedestrians cross the road.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are marked with white lines to show where pedestrians should cross. Some crosswalks are unmarked but still designated for pedestrian use.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn from that lane.
Get ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the protected green arrow is ending. Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: Why should you not stop suddenly in front of large trucks and buses?

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles require longer stopping distances than smaller cars. A sudden stop in front of them may cause a collision because the driver cannot brake in time.

questions.question: Which of these contributes to traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding or driving too fast for conditions.
Getting enough sleep and staying alert.
Paying attention to the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding or driving too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding and driving too fast for road conditions cause many crashes. Always drive at safe speeds within legal limits and adjust for traffic and weather.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce road rage?

options.text: Always signal when changing lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Use your horn frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, follow all traffic laws and signals. Always use your turn signal when changing lanes to show other drivers your intentions.

questions.question: Your reaction time becomes slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your vision, alertness, and judgment. It also makes it harder to judge distances and speeds.
